title: Parrot Catapult & Duck Target Range
description: A medieval-style catapult launches a Parrot projectile toward floating Duck targets arranged at varying distances and heights. The user adjusts launch angle, power, and lateral aim using sliders, then fires the Parrot which follows a realistic parabolic trajectory under gravity and air drag. Hitting a Duck triggers a ragdoll-style knockback with angular momentum transfer, and a scoreboard tracks accuracy and distance.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader from CDN. Load Parrot.glb as the projectile and Duck.glb as targets. Scene setup: a ground plane with grid texture, a simple catapult structure built from BoxGeometry at the left side, and 5 Duck targets placed at varying distances (15-60 units) and heights (0-15 units) on the right side. Each Duck should slowly bob up and down using sine-wave animation. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 12, 30) looking at the catapult, with OrbitControls enabled. Lighting: DirectionalLight with shadows enabled, plus ambient light. Create an HTML overlay panel with three sliders: Launch Angle (15-75 degrees), Power (10-50 units), and Lateral Aim (-15 to 15 degrees), plus a Fire button and a Reset button. When Fire is clicked: clone the Parrot model, place it on the catapult arm, animate the catapult arm rotating forward, then release the Parrot as a physics projectile. Implement custom physics in the animation loop: apply gravity (9.81 m/s²), optional air drag coefficient (0.02), and compute parabolic trajectory each frame using velocity vectors derived from angle, power, and lateral aim. The Parrot should rotate along its velocity vector during flight. Implement AABB collision detection between the flying Parrot and each Duck. On collision: remove the Duck with a particle burst effect using 30 small spheres that scatter outward with random velocities and fade out, increment a hit counter displayed on screen, and show the distance traveled. If the Parrot hits the ground without hitting a Duck, display a miss indicator showing where it landed. Track total shots fired and hits in a scoreboard div. After all 5 Ducks are hit, display a completion message with accuracy percentage. The Reset button restores all Ducks and resets the score. Validate that angle, power, and aim values are within their defined ranges before allowing a launch. Add trajectory preview as a dotted line that updates in real-time as sliders change.
